title: Cornelius' vision (Acts 10:1–33)
hook: some guests you plan for. some arrive at the gate while lunch is still cooking
tomorrow: what's the first thing Peter says in a stranger's house?

segments.voice: A week of Acts on the move: Stephen's two prayers, a gift not for sale, a reader on a desert road, scales, a basket over a wall, and the coats Tabitha made. Yesterday's line: full of good works.
screen: `FULL OF GOOD WORKS.` → `A WEEK OF ACTS ON THE MOVE.`

segments.voice: Some guests you plan for for weeks. Some knock at the gate while lunch is still on the stove. Today has both, in two cities. In Caesarea lives a Roman officer, Cornelius, "A devout man, and one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway." An angel tells him to send to Joppa for a man named Peter, so the soldier sends for the fisherman. The next day in Joppa, Peter goes up on a roof to pray, "And he became very hungry, and would have eaten."
screen: `GUESTS AT THE GATE.` → `A SOLDIER WHO PRAYED ALWAY.` → `A HUNGRY MAN ON A ROOF.`

segments.voice: While the meal is cooking, Peter sees something like a great sheet let down from heaven, full of all kinds of animals, and hears: "Rise, Peter; kill, and eat." He refuses: "Not so, Lord; for I have never eaten any thing that is common or unclean." He has kept the food laws faithfully, and he says so. The voice answers: "What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common." Three times, and the sheet goes back up. Peter is still puzzling when the men from Cornelius knock at the gate. He calls them in and gives them a place to stay. A day later he walks into the house of a Gentile, full of Cornelius' relatives and friends, and tells them what the sheet meant. It wasn't about lunch: "God hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean." Any man. Two visions, two cities, and a door opened from both sides.
screen: `A SHEET, THREE TIMES.` · `NOT SO, LORD.` · `NOT ABOUT LUNCH.` · `CALL NO MAN COMMON.` · then, large: `WHAT GOD HAS CLEANSED.`

segments.voice: For the sit, listen for the sounds that reach you from outside: a car, footsteps, a dog, the wind. Don't sort them into welcome and unwelcome. Let each one arrive and pass, the way Peter heard the knock at the gate and called the strangers in.
Cornelius' vision. A Roman centurion is told to send for Peter, while Peter has a vision of his own.
Your line: what god has cleansed, heard on a roof and lived at a door. Week done.
